questions.question: What are (3) key tasks involved in the process of stripping beds?

questions.question: What are five (5) tasks involved in the making of beds?
guidance: Answer may address, but is not limited to, five of the following:
Ensure electric blanket is intact and undamaged, straight and secured.
Ensure mattress protector is straight and secured.

Place the bottom sheet on first with the seams at the edges down (if the bottom sheet is a fitted sheet then it will just be fitted to the bed). Work from preferred side of bed by putting clean, folded sheet in middle of bed on top of mattress protector.
Unfold half of sheet then go to other side and repeat.
Fold and tuck bottom sheet in at top end, completing with ‘hospital folds’ on both sides and smooth out any creases or loose parts of the sheet.
Fit the top sheet in a similar fashion to the bottom sheet by laying the top sheet in middle of bed on top of bottom sheet, then fold over at the correct height for the standard guest.
Work from preferred side and unfold half of this sheet, going to other side to repeat and smooth out any creases or loose parts of the sheet.
Fold and tuck top sheet in at the foot end of bed, finishing off with hospital corners on both sides.
Add blankets fitting the blankets with the hospital or mitre tuck at the foot of the bed and smooth out blankets so there are no creases.
Position bedspread, duvet or doona according to the venue requirements, ensuring that buttons, fastening clips or zippers are at the foot of the bed.
Place runner across foot of bed with bottom edge 30cms from bottom – ensure there is an even overhang on both sides of the bed.

Place clean pillowcases on all pillows, then ‘plump’ each pillow and place on the bed according to the room and bed presentation procedure. Put pillows on bed, with bottom pillows being placed flat and top ones standing against bed head.
Check and adjust or smooth out any creases as needed to produce a neat and wrinkle-free appearance so the bed is presented professionally according to the establishment's standards.

questions.question: What are three (3) manual handling techniques to be mindful of when making beds?
guidance: Answer may address, but is not limited to, three of the following:
Avoid bending over for longer than necessary - mix up tasks that require bending with tasks that can be completed with an upright posture.
When lifting, bend your legs rather than your back.
If a load is too heavy for your own arm strength, avoid strain on your back by lightening the load or getting assistance.
Avoid twisting or sudden, sharp movements.
Adjust mattresses with your leg and not with your back.
Walk around the bed to work from each side rather than bend across the bed.
answer_instructions: Answer may address, but is not limited to, three of the following:
answer_points: Avoid bending over for longer than necessary - mix up tasks that require bending with tasks that can be completed with an upright posture.

questions.question: What are four (4) ways you may be required to report a hazard in a guest room?

Informal, verbal reports to a manager or work health and safety representative (HSR), for example, face-to-face or via phone

questions.question: What are three (3) factors a housekeeper should take into account when selecting equipment to clean rooms?
guidance: Answer may address, but is not limited to, three of the following:
Functions required to service and clean rooms, for example, dusting, stain removal and cleaning wet or dry surfaces
Suitability for the size of cleaning areas and the nature of floor surfaces and soft furnishings
Time and cost efficiency in its use
Ease of use and maintenance
Reliability and durability
Versatility - a piece of equipment with more than one function means less equipment for housekeeping attendants to move
Portability - for ease of movement between rooms and establishment floors, for example, equipment with wheels
Meeting work health and safety requirements, such as electrical and mechanical safety or physical safety, such as the weight of an item
